get.description:
Report that the process is running.

Deliberately dependency-free. A liveness probe that checks the database turns
a dependency outage into a restart loop.

Report whether the process can serve traffic.

Checks only critical infrastructure: the database. Object storage, AI
providers and messaging are optional dependencies by design, so their
unavailability must not take an instance out of rotation.
Return the counters and totals in the exposition format.

get.summary: A business's public shop and its catalogue
get.description: Return a published shop, for a caller with no account and no token.

get.summary: One product of a public shop
get.description:
Return one published product of a published shop, for a caller with no account.

Declared after the shop route and with a longer path, so the shop page is matched exactly and
a product address cannot be confused with a business address.

post.summary: Send a list to a shop
post.description:
Take a customer's list. No account, and no answer about the shop's own affairs.

The response says the list arrived and how many lines it has. It does not say whether anything
is in
stock, what anything costs the shop, or whether this customer has ordered before - none of which
is a
customer's business, and the first of which the product owner settled explicitly: an Igbo trader
is
never truly out of stock, he goes and finds it.

get.summary: Open an invoice through a shared link
get.description: Return the invoice a token opens, for a caller with no account and no token of their own.

get.summary: Open an exported report through a shared link
get.description:
Redirect the holder to the artifact.

A redirect rather than a stream: the bytes never travel through the application process, and
the URL is the provider's own short-lived one, so a link shared onward stops working when the
object's URL expires. The address is built by the provider that holds the object, not by a
guess about which one it is.

Declared before the invoice route so a token can never be read as a path segment; a report token
is opaque and carries no meaning, which is the point.

post.summary: Create an account and sign in
post.description:
Register a user, returning a session so no second request is needed.

The session is also written to cookies, so a browser is signed in without any
client code holding a token. The body keeps carrying the tokens for clients
that have no cookie jar.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a session
post.description: Sign in with an email address or a phone number.

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token into a new session
post.description:
Rotate the presented refresh token, from the body or from the cookie.

The presented token is revoked as part of the exchange, so a token that is
used twice is recognised as reuse and ends the whole session family.

post.summary: End the session behind a refresh token
post.description:
Sign out, ending the session and clearing the cookies.

Idempotent: an unknown or already-revoked token still produces success, so a
client that has lost track of its session can reach a signed-out state. The
cookies are cleared either way, because a browser that keeps a dead cookie
keeps looking signed in.

post.summary: Change the authenticated user's password
post.description: Change the caller's password and end their other sessions.

get.summary: Read the authenticated user's own profile
get.description: Return the caller's own profile.

delete.summary: Deactivate the authenticated user's own account
delete.description:
Deactivate the caller's own account.

A `DELETE` that deactivates rather than deletes: business history references
this person, and the response body reports the resulting state so a client
does not have to guess whether the account is gone or merely inactive.

patch.summary: Update the authenticated user's own profile

would make the device re-apply changes it has already applied.

get.description: Return this device's position, or zero when it has never synchronized.

CustomerCreateSchema.description: A customer a business is recording.

decides whether it is the same customer, and blocking the write would push them into
inventing a phone number to get past it.

CustomerUpdateSchema.description:
A partial edit of a customer.

Every field is optional, and `exclude_unset` preserves the difference between "not
sent" and "sent as null": clearing a phone number, an address or notes is a real
operation, and leaving one alone is a different request. `version` is the one field
that is not a customer attribute - it is what the caller was working from.

A period's trading, day by day and in total.

Days with no sales are absent rather than zero: the caller knows the period it asked for, and
filling gaps here would be the API deciding what a chart draws.

A client presenting itself.

The same request registers a new installation and renews a known one: a client
cannot tell its first launch from its hundredth, and it should not have to.

DeviceResponseSchema.description:
One installation, as the business sees it.

The identifier is not returned. An operator needs to know that a device is
registered, who it belongs to and when it was last seen; the opaque string adds
nothing and is not theirs to hold.

DeviceRevocationResponseSchema.title: DeviceRevocationResponseSchema
DeviceRevocationResponseSchema.description:
The result of revoking a device.

The session count is reported because it is the part that matters: a revocation
that ended no sessions is worth noticing, since it means the phone had none.

ExpenseCategoryListSchema.description: The declared vocabulary, so a client chooses instead of guessing.

ExpenseCreateSchema.title: ExpenseCreateSchema
ExpenseCreateSchema.description:
An expense a business is recording.

`incurred_at` is optional and means "now" when absent: most expenses are recorded as they
are paid, and a back-dated one is the case that has to say so. It must carry a timezone,
because a bare local time means a different instant to every client that sends one.

ExpensePushPayload.title: ExpensePushPayload
ExpensePushPayload.description: What an expense needs to be recorded.

ExpenseResponseSchema.title: ExpenseResponseSchema
ExpenseResponseSchema.description:
One expense, as the business recorded it.

The amount is a decimal string: `money_text` is the one wire format for money in this
product, and a JSON number would let a client's float arithmetic disagree with the
ledger. `counted_amount` is included because a reversed expense is still in the list and
a client that shows spending should not have to know that reversal means zero.

InventoryMovementResponseSchema.description:
One ledger entry, as a business sees it.

`is_overdraw` is published because it is the fact a business with a permissive policy
needs to find: the movements that took stock below zero, without reading every row.

InventoryStateResponseSchema.title: InventoryStateResponseSchema
InventoryStateResponseSchema.description: One product's stock numbers, without the product.

InvitationResponseSchema.title: InvitationResponseSchema
InvitationResponseSchema.description:
An invitation as an owner sees it.

`token` is present only in the response that creates the invitation. The
digest is what is stored, so this is the single moment the value exists in a
response, and the owner is expected to pass it on through whatever channel they
already use to talk to that worker.

IssuedShareLinkResponseSchema.title: IssuedShareLinkResponseSchema
IssuedShareLinkResponseSchema.description:
A freshly minted link, and the token that opens it.

The only response in this product that carries a token, and it carries it once. A caller that
loses it asks for a new link: the server cannot re-show it, because the server did not keep it.

LoginSchema.title: LoginSchema
LoginSchema.description:
A credential exchange.

One `identifier` field rather than separate email and phone fields: a trader
types whichever they remember, and the service decides which it is. The
response to a failure is identical either way, so the shape reveals nothing.

LogoutSchema.title: LogoutSchema
LogoutSchema.description:
The response to a sign-out.

A fixed message rather than an empty body: a client that receives nothing has
to guess whether the request succeeded.

LowStockProductSchema.title: LowStockProductSchema
LowStockProductSchema.description: A product at or below the threshold its business set.

MembershipInviteSchema.title: MembershipInviteSchema
MembershipInviteSchema.description: An invitation to join a business.

MembershipRoleUpdateSchema.title: MembershipRoleUpdateSchema
MembershipRoleUpdateSchema.description: A role change for an existing member.

MembershipStatus.title: MembershipStatus
MembershipStatus.description: The lifecycle of one person's access to one business.

MembershipStatusUpdateSchema.title: MembershipStatusUpdateSchema
MembershipStatusUpdateSchema.description:
A status change for an existing member.

Only the two states an administrative action can reach are accepted: returning
somebody to active, or suspending them. Removal is a DELETE, and an invitation
is not a status a person can be moved back to.

NegativeStockPolicy.title: NegativeStockPolicy
NegativeStockPolicy.description: What happens when a movement would take a product below zero.

NotificationCountSchema.title: NotificationCountSchema
NotificationCountSchema.description: How many notifications this person has not read here.

NotificationResponseSchema.title: NotificationResponseSchema
NotificationResponseSchema.description: One notification, as the person it is for sees it.

NotificationType.title: NotificationType
NotificationType.description:
What kind of thing this is.

A closed set. A notification type a client does not recognise is a notification it cannot
render, and the type is what a client keys its icon and its routing off.

PasswordChangedSchema.title: PasswordChangedSchema
PasswordChangedSchema.description: The response to a password change.

PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod
PaymentMethod.description: How the money arrived. Only what this product can actually accept.

PaymentResponseSchema.title: PaymentResponseSchema
PaymentResponseSchema.description: One payment, with its amount and what has happened to it since.

PendingInvitationSchema.title: PendingInvitationSchema
PendingInvitationSchema.description:
An invitation as the invited person sees it.

Names the business and the role and nothing more: the invitee has not joined
yet, so they are not entitled to the business's details until they accept.

ProductCreateSchema.title: ProductCreateSchema
ProductCreateSchema.description: A product a business is adding to its catalogue.

ProductImageOrderSchema.title: ProductImageOrderSchema
ProductImageOrderSchema.description: A new gallery order, given as the complete list of image identifiers.

ProductImageReconciliationResponseSchema.title: ProductImageReconciliationResponseSchema
ProductImageReconciliationResponseSchema.description: What a reconciliation pass managed to clean up.

ProductImageRemovalResponseSchema.title: ProductImageRemovalResponseSchema
ProductImageRemovalResponseSchema.description:
The result of removing an image.

`storage_released` is the part worth reading: when the provider delete failed, the
bytes are still stored and still counted against the tenant, and the image is marked
for reconciliation instead of the row disappearing. A caller that only saw "200 OK"
would have no way to know a leak was left behind.

ProductImageResponseSchema.title: ProductImageResponseSchema
ProductImageResponseSchema.description:
One stored picture, as the business sees it.

`delivery_url` is present only when the adapter could build one. A tenant on a
private provider gets no public URL, and the schema says so with null rather than
inventing a link that does not resolve.

ProductPerformanceSchema.title: ProductPerformanceSchema
ProductPerformanceSchema.description: What one product sold in a period.

ProductResponseSchema.title: ProductResponseSchema
ProductResponseSchema.description:
One product, as the business sees it.

Prices are Decimal, which this API serialises as a JSON string: a client receives
`"250.00"` and never a binary approximation of it.

ProductShareSheetSchema.title: ProductShareSheetSchema
ProductShareSheetSchema.description:
Everything a share button needs, in one response.

The public URL, the string a QR code should encode, and the WhatsApp link with the message
already written. One response rather than three: the three describe one intention, and a client
that fetched them separately would render a share sheet with a stale address in it.

`whatsapp_url` is null when the business has no number a customer can message, and
`whatsapp_unavailable_reason` says why. A typed absence rather than a silent null: a button that
does nothing is worse than one that explains itself.

ProductUpdateSchema.title: ProductUpdateSchema
ProductUpdateSchema.description:
A partial edit of a product.

Every field is optional, and `exclude_unset` preserves the difference between "not
sent" and "sent as null": clearing a description, a category, a SKU or a cost is a
real operation, and leaving one alone is a different request. The two lifecycle
booleans are absent - publication and deactivation have their own operations.

PublicProductPageSchema.title: PublicProductPageSchema
PublicProductPageSchema.description:
One product of a shop, with the shop it belongs to named.

The shop's name travels with the product because a shared link to a product is how most people
arrive: a page that says "Rice 50kg" and nothing about who is selling it is a page a customer
cannot act on.

PublicProductSchema.title: PublicProductSchema
PublicProductSchema.description: One product, as a stranger sees it.

PublicRequestAcceptedSchema.title: PublicRequestAcceptedSchema
PublicRequestAcceptedSchema.description: What a customer is told: that it arrived, and nothing about the shop's own affairs.

PublicRequestLineSchema.title: PublicRequestLineSchema
PublicRequestLineSchema.description:
One thing a customer is asking for.

Either something from the catalogue - which carries a price they could see - or free text with
their
own words, because in real life nothing stops a customer asking for what the shop has not
listed.
An unpriced line is normal: the customer does not price what the trader has to go and find.

PublicRequestSchema.title: PublicRequestSchema
PublicRequestSchema.description: A list as it arrives from somebody with no account.

PublicStorefrontSchema.title: PublicStorefrontSchema
PublicStorefrontSchema.description: A shop, as a stranger sees it.

RefreshSessionSchema.title: RefreshSessionSchema
RefreshSessionSchema.description:
A refresh request.

The token is optional because a browser does not send it here: it arrives in
an HttpOnly cookie the page cannot read, and a script or a mobile client
sends it in the body as before. A request that carries neither is refused by
the route, which is the one place that can see both.

lifetime_days.title: Lifetime Days
lifetime_days.description: How long the share link lasts.

ReportExportRequestSchema.title: ReportExportRequestSchema
ReportExportRequestSchema.description:
A request to write a report out as a file.

The period is optional for the same reason it is optional on a read, and the bounds are the
service's: a schema that defaulted one would be a second opinion about what "this week" means.

ReportExportResponseSchema.title: ReportExportResponseSchema
ReportExportResponseSchema.description:
A written-out report, and the link that opens it.

`token` is the only copy: the server stores a digest, so a client that loses the link asks for a
new export rather than expecting the server to re-show it.

ReportType.title: ReportType
ReportType.description:
Which report an artifact holds.

A closed set: an export of a report this version does not have is a file nobody can read, and
the
name is what a client uses to decide how to render it.

RequestLineResponseSchema.title: RequestLineResponseSchema
RequestLineResponseSchema.description: One line of a list, as the trader sees it.

RequestLineState.title: RequestLineState
RequestLineState.description:
What the trader found when he went looking.

`SOMEWHERE` is the state everything starts in and it is not a promise of stock: an Igbo trader
is
never truly out of stock, and a customer is never shown whether something is on the shelf.

RequestLineUnit.title: RequestLineUnit
RequestLineUnit.description: How a line is counted. A piece or a pack of them, and nothing in between.

RequestLineWorkSchema.title: RequestLineWorkSchema
RequestLineWorkSchema.description:
What the trader says about one line: where he got it, what it cost, what he charges.

Every field is optional and the difference between "not sent" and "sent as null" is preserved: a
price sent as null is not a price, a cost sent as null clears what he had recorded, and a state
sent
as null leaves it where it is.

RequestResponseSchema.title: RequestResponseSchema
RequestResponseSchema.description: A list, as the business sees it - with its lines and what they come to.

RequestStatus.title: RequestStatus
RequestStatus.description:
Where a list has got to.

A customer sends it, the trader prices it, and then he confirms it - which is the single moment
a
wish becomes a sale. Cancelling is possible until it is confirmed, and not after: a confirmed
list
is a record of an agreement, and ending it is a refund or a return rather than a cancellation.

RolePermissionsUpdateSchema.title: RolePermissionsUpdateSchema
RolePermissionsUpdateSchema.description: A replacement permission set for a role.

RoleResponseSchema.title: RoleResponseSchema
RoleResponseSchema.description:
One role and the capabilities it grants.

The permission codes are included rather than the identifiers, because a
client renders a role by what it can do.

SaleCancellationSchema.title: SaleCancellationSchema
SaleCancellationSchema.description:
Why a sale was cancelled, and nothing else.

A client may not send a status, a refund amount or a restock quantity: those are
consequences the service derives from the sale, and accepting one would let a caller
decide what the books say.

SaleCreateSchema.title: SaleCreateSchema
SaleCreateSchema.description: A whole sale in one request.

SaleCreationResponseSchema.title: SaleCreationResponseSchema
SaleCreationResponseSchema.description:
The receipt, and whether this request produced it or found it.

`was_replayed` tells a client that its basket had already been recorded: the receipt
returned is the original one, and a client can show it again rather than ringing the sale
up twice.

SaleItemResponseSchema.title: SaleItemResponseSchema
SaleItemResponseSchema.description: One line of a receipt, with the name and the price as they were at the time.

SaleLinePushSchema.title: SaleLinePushSchema
SaleLinePushSchema.description: One line of a sale recorded offline.

SaleLineRequestSchema.title: SaleLineRequestSchema
SaleLineRequestSchema.description:
One thing being sold.

`unit_price` is optional because the usual case is the product's current price. When a
price is sent it is what is charged and what is snapshotted - a negotiated price is a
real thing at a counter - and the product's own price is not consulted.

SalePaymentPushSchema.title: SalePaymentPushSchema
SalePaymentPushSchema.description: Money taken for a sale recorded offline.

SalePushPayload.title: SalePushPayload
SalePushPayload.description: What a sale needs to be completed.

SaleResponseSchema.title: SaleResponseSchema
SaleResponseSchema.description:
One sale as a business sees it, with its lines and its payments.

The lines and the payments belong in the response rather than behind a second request:
this is a receipt, and a receipt a client has to assemble from three calls is a receipt
that can be shown half-finished.

SaleSummaryResponseSchema.title: SaleSummaryResponseSchema
SaleSummaryResponseSchema.description:
One sale in a list, without its lines or payments.

A day's sales are read as a list of receipts, and loading every line of every sale to
render that list is the query that makes a sales screen slow.

ShareLinkCreateSchema.title: ShareLinkCreateSchema
ShareLinkCreateSchema.description: A request to share one invoice.

ShareLinkResponseSchema.title: ShareLinkResponseSchema
ShareLinkResponseSchema.description: A link a business has created, without the token that opens it.

ShareableResource.title: ShareableResource
ShareableResource.description:
What a link can open.

A closed set. Shipments join it when that module exists; naming them now would let a caller
mint a link to a record this product cannot serve, and the failure would be discovered by the
customer who opened it.

SharedInvoiceLineSchema.title: SharedInvoiceLineSchema
SharedInvoiceLineSchema.description: One line of a shared invoice.

SharedInvoiceSchema.title: SharedInvoiceSchema
SharedInvoiceSchema.description: An invoice opened through a link, for a caller with no account.

SpendingByCategorySchema.title: SpendingByCategorySchema
SpendingByCategorySchema.description:
What the business spent per category in a period.

Values are decimal strings, and a category with no spending is absent rather than zero:
the vocabulary endpoint tells a client what the headings are, and inventing zero rows
here would be this layer deciding what a report displays.

The total comes from the service. Summing the mapping here would be arithmetic in a
transport handler, and a handler that rounds is a handler whose total disagrees with the
ledger.

StockAdjustmentPushPayload.title: StockAdjustmentPushPayload
StockAdjustmentPushPayload.description:
A counted correction, as a delta rather than an absolute quantity.

A delta is what makes this operation-based: two devices counting the same shelf each record
what they found as a change from what the server held, and neither can silently overwrite the
other's count the way an absolute quantity would.

StockAdjustmentSchema.title: StockAdjustmentSchema
StockAdjustmentSchema.description: A correction after a count, in either direction, with its reason.

StockChangeResponseSchema.title: StockChangeResponseSchema
StockChangeResponseSchema.description: A movement and the state it produced.

StockDamageSchema.title: StockDamageSchema
StockDamageSchema.description: Stock that can no longer be sold.

StockReceiptPushPayload.title: StockReceiptPushPayload
StockReceiptPushPayload.description: Stock that arrived while the device was offline.

StockTransferSchema.title: StockTransferSchema
StockTransferSchema.description: Stock moving from one product record to another inside one business.

StorefrontPublishSchema.title: StorefrontPublishSchema
StorefrontPublishSchema.description: What a business says about its shop when it opens it.

StorefrontResponseSchema.title: StorefrontResponseSchema
StorefrontResponseSchema.description: The business's own view of its shop.

StorefrontUpdateSchema.title: StorefrontUpdateSchema
StorefrontUpdateSchema.description: A partial edit of what the shop says. It never changes whether the shop is open.

SyncChangeSchema.title: SyncChangeSchema
SyncChangeSchema.description:
One change a device must fetch.

The feed names records rather than carrying them: a client fetches the current record through
the endpoint that owns it, which already checks the permission and already knows the wire
format. A payload here would be a second representation of the domain that can disagree with
the first.

SyncCursorRequestSchema.title: SyncCursorRequestSchema
SyncCursorRequestSchema.description: How far the device has applied.

SyncCursorResponseSchema.title: SyncCursorResponseSchema
SyncCursorResponseSchema.description: The position the device now holds.

SyncOperationStatus.title: SyncOperationStatus
SyncOperationStatus.description: What the server did with the operation.

SyncPullRequestSchema.title: SyncPullRequestSchema
SyncPullRequestSchema.description: How far the device has read, and how much it wants.

SyncPullResponseSchema.title: SyncPullResponseSchema
SyncPullResponseSchema.description: A page of changes, and where the business's feed has reached.

SyncPushRequestSchema.title: SyncPushRequestSchema
SyncPushRequestSchema.description: A queue of operations, in the order the device recorded them.

SyncPushResponseSchema.title: SyncPushResponseSchema
SyncPushResponseSchema.description: Every operation's answer, in the order they were pushed.

TenantResponseSchema.title: TenantResponseSchema
TenantResponseSchema.description: A business as its members see it.

TenantStockPolicyUpdateSchema.title: TenantStockPolicyUpdateSchema
TenantStockPolicyUpdateSchema.description:
The business's rule about stock going negative.

A deliberate operation rather than a profile field: a business that starts permitting
negative stock is changing what its own numbers mean, and the change should appear as
its own act rather than inside a form submission that also fixed a phone number.

TenantSummarySchema.title: TenantSummarySchema
TenantSummarySchema.description:
A business as it appears in a list of the caller's businesses.

Narrower than the full view: a picker needs a name, a link and whether the
business is active, not the address and the contact details.

TenantUpdateSchema.title: TenantUpdateSchema
TenantUpdateSchema.description:
A business profile update.

The slug is absent and therefore rejected by `extra="forbid"`: it is published
on links that already exist, so changing it is not a profile edit. A business
that genuinely needs a different public name gets a new slug through an
explicit, audited operation, not by sending one to this endpoint.

UserProfileUpdateSchema.title: UserProfileUpdateSchema
UserProfileUpdateSchema.description:
A partial profile update.

Every field is optional: the request describes what to change, and an omitted
field means "leave it alone". `extra="forbid"` rejects an unknown field
instead of ignoring it, so a client that misspells a field learns immediately
rather than believing it saved something.

UserResponseSchema.title: UserResponseSchema
UserResponseSchema.description:
The user as a client sees it.

There is no password hash here, and there never will be: a test asserts that
no field name in this schema is credential-shaped. Email and phone are
present because this is the caller's own profile, which they already know.

HTTPBearer.description: The access_token returned by /api/v1/auth/login or /api/v1/auth/register. A browser does not need this: it is already signed in by an HttpOnly session cookie.
